children: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore oil and gas block from Vedanta Oil & Gas following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies.

Vedanta, led by billionaire Anil Agarwal, has recognised an impairment charge of around Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block, reflecting the financial impact of losing operational control.

The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on 22 July 2026, after a single-judge bench of the Delhi High Court dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing.
The block was previously operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest. ONGC held 50 per cent, while Invenire Petrodyne owned the remaining 10 per cent.

The government, through a letter dated 19 September 2025, had declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC. Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court on 22 September 2025.

The production-sharing contract for the Cambay block expired on 29 June 2023. Vedanta and its joint venture partners had applied for an extension on 28 June 2021 under the government's 2017 extension policy.

The company's legal challenge had resulted in an interim order directing the parties to maintain status quo over the block. However, the High Court dismissed Vedanta's writ petition on 22 July 2026, leading to the vacation of the interim protection.
Following the ruling, ONGC took over the block and applied for a petroleum lease on 28 July 2026.
The takeover marks a change in operational control of the offshore asset after the dispute over the government's decision to deny an extension of the production-sharing contract.
Vedanta's impairment charge of Rs 379 crore relates to assets and receivables associated with the block, according to the company's regulatory filing.
